whenToUse: Something arrives or changes: a page switch, a list that loads, a KPI that updates, content that replaces its skeleton.
Website sections below the fold (Reveal, Stagger) and number bands (CountUp), with one SiteShell motion level for the whole site.
Admin screens: a fade or a 6–8 px rise on a list or KPI row, SkeletonSwap for loaded data, CountUp on the one figure that matters.
One expressive moment per screen, such as a word-by-word hero heading on a portfolio site at the full level.
avoidWhen: Settled UI that does not change: tables, forms, toolbars, navigation and settings pages stay still.
Anything above the fold on first load: the hero enters with CSS on first paint, never with a scroll reveal.
Parallax, Tilt, Magnetic or TextReveal inside an admin app.
Animating width, height, top or margin, or writing your own keyframes: use the kit primitives (opacity and transform only).
a11y: prefers-reduced-motion and data-motion="off" render every primitive in its final state.
Moving content (Ticker, marquee) has a pause control and stops on hover and focus.
CountUp renders and announces the final value; TextReveal is read as one string.
Content already on screen at load is never hidden again, so there is no flash and no layout shift.
